citations.B1: Read-then-write on `counts` is not atomic, so concurrent threads both see `count < limit` and both increment
citations.B2: both increment, letting users exceed the limit and losing updates
citations.B3: guard the check-and-increment with a lock or use an atomic increment
citations.B4: There is no time window, so counts never reset and a user who hits 100 is blocked forever; add a window
citations.B5: The dict grows by one entry per user ID and is never evicted, so memory grows without bound
citations.B6: `counts` lives in one process's memory, so each worker keeps its own copy and the effective limit is `limit × workers`
citations.B7: A `None` or shared anonymous `user_id` ... and an unhashable ID raises `TypeError`; normalize the key ... and validate it
